record.paper_title: Towards Event-Triggered NMPC for Efficient 6G Communications: Experimental Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: How should the event-triggering threshold ε be selected for an event-triggered nonlinear model predictive controller so that the controller balances closed-loop cost against wireless communication demand for a given application and channel condition? In the reported Furuta-pendulum experiment, ε = 0 corresponds to periodic control with 100% communication demand, increasing ε makes recalculations less frequent and raises closed-loop cost while lowering transmissions, and ε = 0.4 was suitable for that benchmark; the broader design question is how to choose such thresholds systematically for other requirements.

evidence.quote: A threshold of ε = 0 corresponds to periodic control and, therefore, a communication demand of 100 %. With increasing ε, the recalculation of the closed-loop solution becomes less frequent, and the open-loop control input is applied for a longer duration, resulting in a higher closed-loop cost, as illustrated in Figure 5.

On the other hand, this reduces the frequency of control signal transmissions over the wireless interface, thereby lowering the communication demand. Depending on the application requirements, we observe the best trade-off between control performance and communication demand.
For the Furuta pendulum, we consider ε = 0.4 as a suitable threshold. In this case, the communication demand is reduced to 55 % network traffic with a negligible impact on the control performance.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a continuous-time nonlinear plant
  ẋ(t) = f(x(t), u(t)),  x(t) ∈ R^n, u(t) ∈ U ⊂ R^m,
controlled by a nonlinear model predictive controller (NMPC) that, at each triggering instant t_k, solves a finite-horizon optimal control problem
  minimize ∫_{t_k}^{t_k+T} ℓ(x(τ), u(τ)) dτ + V_f(x(t_k+T))
  s.t. ẋ(τ) = f(x(τ), u(τ)), u(τ) ∈ U, x(t_k) = x_meas(t_k),
producing an optimal open-loop input u*(·; t_k). The controller communicates u*(·; t_k) to the actuator over a wireless channel and the actuator applies it in open loop until the next trigger.

Let x̂(τ; t_k) denote the predicted state generated by the model from x_meas(t_k) under u*(·; t_k). The next trigger time t_{k+1} is defined by the event-triggering rule
  t_{k+1} = inf { t > t_k : ‖x_meas(t) − x̂(t; t_k)‖ ≥ ε },
with a fixed threshold ε ≥ 0. Define the long-run closed-loop cost
  J(ε) = limsup_{T→∞} (1/T) ∫_0^T ℓ(x(τ), u(τ)) dτ
and the communication demand
  C(ε) = limsup_{K→∞} (number of triggers in [0, t_K]) / (number of periodic transmissions in [0, t_K]) ∈ [0, 1],
where the denominator corresponds to a fixed periodic sampling baseline (so C(0) = 1).

Provide a systematic procedure that, given:
  (i) the plant dynamics f, stage cost ℓ, terminal cost V_f, input constraint set U, and horizon T;
  (ii) a stochastic model of the wireless channel (e.g., a packet-loss/delay distribution or a capacity constraint);
  (iii) an application-specified weighting between control performance and communication usage, e.g. a scalarization J(ε) + λ C(ε) with λ ≥ 0, or a hard constraint C(ε) ≤ c̄,
selects the threshold ε so that the resulting closed-loop behavior achieves the prescribed trade-off (and, in particular, recovers ε = 0 when λ = 0 and yields ε > 0 that strictly reduces C with a quantified bound on the degradation of J otherwise). The procedure must be applicable across different plants, channel models, and trade-off weightings, not merely tuned by hand for a single benchmark.
artifact.status_search_result: The systematic, application-agnostic selection of the event-triggering threshold ε for nonlinear MPC over wireless channels is identified as an open design problem. Existing literature (e.g., Lehmann et al. 2013, surveys on event-triggered control, and stochastic event-triggering trade-off analyses) provides partial frameworks—mostly for linear systems or specific stochastic settings—but no general systematic threshold-design methodology for nonlinear MPC accounting for arbitrary channel conditions and application requirements has been established.

status_evidence.title: Towards Event-Triggered NMPC for Efficient 6G Communications
status_evidence.snippet: Threshold ε=0 corresponds to periodic control (100% communication); increasing ε reduces transmissions but raises closed-loop cost; ε=0.4 was suitable for the Furuta pendulum.
status_evidence.claim: The systematic selection of ε for general applications and channel conditions is posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Trade-Offs in Stochastic Event-Triggered Control
status_evidence.snippet: Framework for analyzing the trade-off between communication rate and control performance and for optimal tuning of the event threshold.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist for stochastic linear systems but do not provide a general NMPC threshold design.

status_evidence.title: An Introduction to Event-triggered and Self-triggered Control (Heemels et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of event/self-triggered control highlighting threshold design as a key open issue.
status_evidence.claim: General principled threshold design across applications remains an active research direction.
